images.title: Both strips must be 8 cm
images.purpose: Shows rectangle ABCD whose two diagonals, the carpenter's two strips, are both 8 cm long.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rectangle in the centre with its two full diagonals drawn in two colours, each labelled with its length.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle ABCD in thin dark outline, wider than it is tall (about 3 by 2), with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. A small square right angle mark in each of the four corners, in dark outline. The diagonal AC is a thick teal (#0072B2) line from top left to bottom right, with the label 8 cm in teal beside its upper half. The diagonal BD is a thick amber (#E69F00) line from top right to bottom left, with the label 8 cm in amber beside its lower half. The two diagonals cross in the middle with no mark at the crossing. The letters A, B, C, D sit just outside their corners. Under the rectangle, centred, the line AC = BD. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The diagonals of a rectangle are always equal, so the other strip must also be 8 cm.
images.description: Shows rectangle ABCD whose two diagonals, the carpenter's two strips, are both 8 cm long.
images.context: ∆ADC ≅ ∆DAB by SAS (AB = CD, ∠BAD = ∠CDA = 90°, AD common), so AC = BD = 8 cm.

image_decisions.why: Two equal coloured diagonals in one rectangle answer the carpenter's question at a glance.
